summary: Helmer Smith worked in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Lund University (~1927–1936) and Uppsala University (~1936–1947).
Helmut Eimer was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Frank-Richard Hamm (~1968–1973) and held a post as Dr. at the University of Bonn (attested 1991–2010).

Helmut Hoffmann worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Freiburg, Berlin, and under Lüders, Lessing, and Tucci, he held posts at Munich (1948) and Indiana University (1969–1980).

Helmut Krasser worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (~1989–2014) and the University of Vienna (~1989–2014), and served as director of the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.
Helmut Rix studied linguistics and Indology at the University of Würzburg (~1946–1950). He later held posts at the University of Regensburg (~1968–1978) and the University of Freiburg (~1978–1993).

Helmut Tauscher is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ernst Steinkellner. He held a professorship at the University of Vienna (attested 2010–2015) and served as Numata visiting professor at Leiden University.

Helmuth von Glasenapp was an Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hermann Jacobi and Wanczura. He held posts at Bonn, Berlin, the University of Königsberg (1928–1944), and the University of Tübingen (1946–1959).
Hendrik Kern was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Utrecht, Leiden, and under Albrecht Weber, and served as professor at Leiden University from 1865 to 1903.
Heng Sure is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Oakland University, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union (PhD), and was taught by Hsuan Hua and Ronald Y. Nakasone.
Henk Blezer is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University (~1987–1997) and subsequently held a post there (~1997–2009).

Henk Bodewitz was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. He served as dean of the Faculty of Arts at Utrecht (1980–1986) and professor at Leiden University (1992–2002).
Henri Gaidoz worked in linguistics, religious studies, and other fields. He completed studies at the Lycée Louis-le-Grand and studied under Albrecht Weber in 1865.

Henri Maspero was a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and linguistics. Educated at Lycée Montaigne, Lycée Louis-le-Grand, and ENLOV, he held posts at EFEO (1911), the Collège de France (1920–1945), and the Maison Franco-Japonaise (1928–1930).
Henri Pirenne was a historian who studied at Liège, Berlin, Leipzig, Paris, EPHE, and Ghent. He held academic posts at the University of Liège (~1885–1886) and Ghent University (1886–1930).
Henrik Samuel Nyberg was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala University in 1908 and later held a post there (~1919–1956).

Henry Chung-hung Shiu specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Toronto (ending 2006) and studied under Shek-wing Tam, Leonard C. D. C. Priestley, David Waterhouse, and Willard Gurdon Oxtoby.
Henry Clarke Warren worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Harvard and Johns Hopkins and under Charles Rockwell Lanman. He also founded the Harvard Oriental Series.

Henry George Keene worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He held posts at the East India Company (~1798–1811) and as Professor of Arabic, Persian, and Hindústání Literature at East India Company College (~1824–1834).

Henry Herbert Dodwell worked in history, archaeology, and Indology after studying at Lord Williams's School and St John's College. He served in the Indian Educational Service (1908–1922) and was Professor of History of India at SOAS (~1922–1946).
Henry Pitts Forster worked in Indology and linguistics. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (~1783–1815) and was Master of the Calcutta Mint at the India Government Mint, Kolkata (~1803–1815).
